sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Spring Boot interview questions are the single most asked Spring topic — auto-configuration internals, the starter system, application.properties/yml + profiles, Actuator endpoints and security, embedded servers, configuration binding, graceful shutdown, scheduled tasks, layered Docker images, and the troubleshooting questions interviewers pull from real production incidents. This page covers the questions that test whether you have actually shipped Spring Boot to production, not just used start.spring.io. For lower-level Spring concepts (IoC, AOP, transaction internals) see Spring Core; for persistence see Spring Data JPA / Hibernate.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Boot = Spring + opinionated **auto-configuration** + an **embedded server** + **starter** dependencies.

- `@SpringBootApplication` = `@Configuration` + `@EnableAutoConfiguration` + `@ComponentScan`.
- **`spring.factories` / `AutoConfiguration.imports`** — how starters register their config.
- **`@ConditionalOnX`** — what makes auto-config opt-in.
- **`application.properties` / yml + profiles** — environment-aware config.
- **Actuator** — `/actuator/health`, `/info`, `/metrics`, `/env` (secured!).

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Actuator** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Auto configuration** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

- **Embedded servers** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Profiles and properties** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Starters** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Testing** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Troubleshooting** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Disable an auto-config** — `@SpringBootApplication(exclude = ...)` or `spring.autoconfigure.exclude=`.
- **`@ConfigurationProperties` vs `@Value`** — typed binding vs single-key SpEL; prefer the former.
- **Profiles** — comma-separated; `@Profile("!prod")` works; never hardcode secrets.
- **Graceful shutdown** — `server.shutdown=graceful` + `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase`.
- **Layered jars / jib** — Docker-friendly, faster cache hits.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"In Spring Boot I'd lean on the <starter>, override <single property> via `application-<env>.yml`, expose <actuator endpoints> behind <security>, and ship a layered Docker image so dependency layers stay cached. For startup tuning I'd profile with the conditions report and disable unused auto-configs."*
